_comment: Hand-curated track & field records - the third source layer tools/build_records.py merges into the bundled dataset. Levels: world = World Athletics senior outdoor world records; college = US collegiate (NCAA) outdoor records per the Track & Field News lists (cross-verified - TFN's live pages lag, so every mark was confirmed against a second source); high-school = US national high-school outdoor records. Same editorial bar as curated_records.json: every entry verified against the cited source on the as_of date, ratification-pending marks flagged scope='pending', nothing guessed. Times store seconds in value with direction='lower' and the conventional rendering in display; field events are meters, combined events points. High-school throws use lighter implements than college/world (noted per record) - levels are deliberately not cross-comparable.

However, Lancaster HS (TX) ran 43.84 on 2025-03-13 at the Donnie Carter Relays -- the first sub-44 clocking in girls HS history -- and was widely reported by WFAA, NBC DFW, Yahoo Sports, and MileSplit TX as breaking the national record; a later MileSplit TX article reports Lancaster running 43.77 in a subsequent head-to-head vs. Duncanville. Could not confirm why these faster marks are absent from T&FN's official page (ratification lag vs. a wind/timing technicality). Reporting both per user's request to flag discrepancies; treat 44.44 as the last T&FN-confirmed mark and 43.84/43.77 as widely-reported but unconfirmed-by-T&FN as of this research.

records.country: Union Catholic HS, Scotch Plains, NJ
records.meet: New Balance Nationals Outdoor, Franklin Field, Philadelphia, PA
records.notes: Confirmed as the current record on T&FN's live girls-records page (fetched 2026-07-11). NOTE: IMG Academy (FL) ran 8:40.51 at the 2025 Penn Relays -- slower than this mark, so it is a Florida state record, not a new national record, despite some local headlines implying otherwise. A Lake Central HS (IN) tri-meet mark of 8:33.96 appears in some all-time lists but is not T&FN's recognized record (could not confirm ratification status).

records.country: Bishop Gorman HS, Las Vegas, NV
records.notes: This is the OUTDOOR record. Cunningham's more commonly cited 1.99m (6-6 1/4) is an INDOOR mark from March 2016 and is excluded here per outdoor-only scope. Unbroken outdoors since 2015. Corroborated by MileSplit and Las Vegas Review-Journal.

records.meet: World Athletics U20 Championships, Budapest, Hungary
records.notes: Set at an international junior championship (absolute-record convention). T&FN separately lists a 'HS-only competition' record of 4.57m (15-0) by Moll at the Arcadia Invitational (exact date not confirmed during this research, believed circa 2022 season) -- mentioned for completeness, not included as its own entry due to date uncertainty.

records.meet: New Balance Nationals Outdoor, Greensboro, NC
records.notes: Broke the then-oldest-standing US girls HS field record. Unbroken since 2015; no evidence of a challenge found in 2024-2026 searches. Exact date approximate (meet ran June 20-23, 2015). Corroborated by USA Today HSS and MileSplit Maine.

records.country: Merrill F. West HS, Tracy, CA
records.notes: Confirmed as the current record on T&FN's live girls-records page (fetched 2026-07-11), unbroken since 2004. Note: a 2025 California state (CIF) mark by a transgender athlete generated national media controversy but is a state-level record, not the T&FN-recognized national record, and is correctly excluded here.

records.country: Donovan Catholic HS, Toms River, NJ
records.notes: HS girls implement is 4kg shot -- SAME weight used at NCAA/senior international women's level, so comparable across levels (unlike HS boys' 12lb shot). Set at an international junior meet (absolute-record convention); T&FN also lists a 'HS-only competition' record of 17.41m (57-1 1/4) by Wilson at the Ocean County Championships, May 2017, which broke Raven Saunders's 2014 domestic mark of 17.27m (56-7 1/2).

records.meet: USA Junior Track & Field Championships, Bloomington, IN
records.notes: HS girls implement is 1kg discus -- SAME weight used at NCAA/senior international women's level, comparable across levels (unlike HS boys' 1.6kg discus). Vaughan had set an earlier 2012 mark (191-6) at the Texas Relays before this one. Corroborated by maxpreps and her HS student-paper report.

records.country: Connellsville Area Senior HS, Connellsville, PA
records.notes: HS girls implement is 600g javelin -- SAME weight used at senior international women's level, comparable across levels. Broke the prior 2012 mark of 181-2. Unbroken since 2015; no evidence of a challenge found in 2024-2026 searches. Corroborated by Washington Times and USA Today HSS.
